G-F011.trick: Protons = Personal ID (never change). Electrons come and go and change the charge.
G-F011.tip: In atom questions, count each particle separately. Losing a negative electron makes the charge MORE positive.

G-F012.trick: Isotopes = same Protons, different Neutrons. "Neutrons make the Number heavier."
G-F012.tip: Mass number = protons + neutrons. If protons match, any mass difference must come from neutrons.

G-F013.trick: POLAR = a tug-of-war one atom is winning. The winner gets a little negative charge.
G-F013.tip: "Unequal sharing" means polar covalent. Equal sharing means nonpolar, and electrons fully given away make an ionic bond.

G-F014.trick: DEHYDRATION synthesis = building by taking water OUT. HYDROlysis = breaking by putting water IN.
G-F014.tip: Look at what happens to water in the stem. Water removed means joining; water added means splitting.

G-F015.trick: Sugar dissolves but stays whole; salt dissolves AND splits into ions. Only ions carry current.
G-F015.tip: Don't assume "dissolved" means "ionized". Electrolytes split into ions; nonelectrolytes like glucose do not.

G-F016.trick: A buffer is a sponge for H+: it soaks up extra acid so pH barely moves.
G-F016.tip: Buffers resist pH change. They don't stop it completely and they never make it bigger.

G-F017.trick: Plants store STARCH (think potatoes); animals store GLYCOGEN in the liver and muscles.
G-F017.tip: Storage questions often pair plant vs animal forms. Cellulose is plant structure, not storage.

G-F018.trick: Four rings = steroid. CHOLESTEROL is the parent ring that steroid hormones are made from.
G-F018.tip: If the stem mentions rings plus hormone precursors, think steroid lipid: cholesterol.

G-F019.trick: QUATernary = a QUARTET of chains playing together (like hemoglobin's 4 subunits).
G-F019.tip: Primary = sequence, secondary = coils/sheets, tertiary = one chain's 3-D fold, quaternary = more than one chain.

G-F020.trick: ATP = the cell's cash in hand. Fat and glycogen are the savings account.
G-F020.tip: ATP is immediate energy for work like pumps. Pick it over long-term fuel stores when the stem describes active work.

C-ch2-atoms.trick: ATOM = a-TOM (Greek: uncuttable). Smallest piece that still IS that element.
C-ch2-atoms.tip: Atom = keeps an element's identity. Molecule = two or more atoms bonded. Ion = an atom with a charge.

C-ch2-bonds.trick: CATions are PAWsitive (cats have paws). ANions are A Negative ION.
C-ch2-bonds.tip: A positive ion has lost electrons. Na+, K+, Ca2+ are common body cations.

C-ch2-reactions.trick: ANAbolism = ADD on and build. CATAbolism = CUT apart.
C-ch2-reactions.tip: Building big molecules costs energy (anabolism). Breaking them down releases energy (catabolism).

C-ch2-water.tip: Hydrophilic = polar or charged, mixes with water. Hydrophobic = nonpolar, avoids water (like fats).

C-ch2-ph.trick: Lower pH = more H+ = more acid. Each step down is 10× more acidic.
C-ch2-ph.tip: pH runs backward: as H+ goes up, the pH number goes down. Normal blood pH is 7.35–7.45.

C-ch2-carbohydrates.trick: MONO = one sugar. DI = two. POLY = many (a chain like starch).
C-ch2-carbohydrates.tip: Glucose, fructose and galactose are monosaccharides; sucrose and lactose are disaccharides.

C-ch2-lipids.trick: TRI-glyceride = 3 fatty-acid tails on one glycerol, like a 3-pronged fork.
C-ch2-lipids.tip: Triglyceride = energy storage. Phospholipid = 2 tails + phosphate head (membranes). Steroid = rings.

C-ch2-proteins.trick: PEPTIDE bond = the PEPper-glue between amino acids in a chain.
C-ch2-proteins.tip: Peptide bonds are covalent and hold the primary sequence. Folding is held mostly by weaker bonds like hydrogen bonds.

C-ch2-nucleic.trick: DNA = Deoxyribose, double helix, has Thymine. RNA = Ribose, single strand, has Uracil.
C-ch2-nucleic.tip: If the stem says inherited information, pick DNA. RNA carries copies of instructions to make proteins.
